nodes.description: Leucine 130 lies at the end of beta-strand 1 of the central beta-sheet of the NAA80 catalytic domain, with its side chain in a hydrophobic pocket and its backbone participating in the sheet's hydrogen-bond network. Substituting proline removes the backbone amide hydrogen and imposes the ring's steric demands, which was predicted to destabilize the local fold and was then confirmed: recombinant mutant protein is predominantly insoluble where wild-type protein is essentially soluble, and NAA80 protein is severely reduced in patient fibroblasts.

Stable naa80-null lines lose actin N-terminal acetylation essentially completely in skeletal and cardiac muscle, yet develop, swim and feed normally. F0 crispants show smaller otoliths, fewer hair-cell bundles in the lateral crista, shorter stereocilia, reduced hair-cell viability and a reduced acoustic startle response.
